chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Umar ibn Yazid who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man said: I shall surely sit in my house, and I shall pray, and I shall fast, and I shall worship my Lord; as for my livelihood, it shall come to me.'
So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'This is one of the three whose supplications are not answered for them.'

key_terms.الثَّلَاثَة: The three — a reference to a well-known category in hadith literature of three types of people whose du'a is not accepted.
key_terms.رِزْق: Sustenance/livelihood provided by God; the means of living. In Islamic theology, all rizq ultimately comes from God, but the believer is obligated to pursue it through lawful means.
key_terms.لَا يُسْتَجَابُ: Supplications are not answered; the passive form implies God Himself does not respond to their du'a.

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about a person who stays home worshipping without seeking his livelihood?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) is asked about a man who resolves to devote himself entirely to worship while passively expecting his livelihood to arrive without effort. The Imam categorizes this person among three types whose supplications (du'a) are rejected. This teaching reflects the Islamic principle that reliance upon God (tawakkul) must be paired with personal effort and seeking one's livelihood — passive abandonment of one's responsibilities is not genuine tawakkul but rather a form of blameworthy negligence that disqualifies one from divine response to supplication.
